source.name: sp_GetExternalInventory

assumptions: OPENQUERY linked server functionality mapped to PostgreSQL dblink extension
RemoteWarehouse linked server would need to be configured as a foreign server using postgres_fdw or dblink
ProductCode assumed to be TEXT type (could be VARCHAR or other string type)
AvailableStock assumed to be INTEGER type (could be NUMERIC or other numeric type)
The procedure does not return a result set, only prints/logs the SQL statement
PRINT statement converted to RAISE NOTICE for equivalent logging behavior
NVARCHAR(MAX) converted to TEXT as PostgreSQL standard text type
SET NOCOUNT ON has no direct equivalent in PostgreSQL and is omitted (PostgreSQL doesn't send row counts by default in procedures)

reviewFlags.reason: Linked server configuration must be migrated. PostgreSQL requires either postgres_fdw (for PostgreSQL remote servers) or dblink extension. The remote server 'RemoteWarehouse' needs to be set up as a foreign server with appropriate connection details and credentials.
Column data types (ProductCode, AvailableStock) are assumed based on common patterns. Verify actual data types from the remote Inventory table schema and adjust accordingly.
PRINT converted to RAISE NOTICE. Verify that logging behavior meets application requirements. RAISE NOTICE goes to client and server log, while SQL Server PRINT goes to client messages.

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server OPENQUERY requires migration to PostgreSQL foreign data wrapper (postgres_fdw) or dblink extension. Setup and configuration differ significantly. postgres_fdw is recommended for PostgreSQL-to-PostgreSQL connections, while dblink provides more flexibility but requires explicit connection strings.

PRINT statements in SQL Server send messages to the client. RAISE NOTICE in PostgreSQL sends notices that may be handled differently by client applications. Message routing and visibility should be tested.
PostgreSQL procedures do not send row count messages by default, so SET NOCOUNT ON has no equivalent and is not needed.

While this procedure only prints the SQL, if it were to execute dynamically, SQL Server uses EXEC/sp_executesql while PostgreSQL uses EXECUTE. The dblink function executes the query directly on the remote server.
